title: South Crete Highlights
tagline: Preveli Monastery, the palm-forest lagoon and Triopetra beach in one unhurried day.
seoTitle: Preveli Palm Beach & Monastery Tour from Rethymno
seoDescription: A six-hour private day trip from Rethymno to Preveli Monastery, the Preveli palm forest and lagoon, Triopetra beach and Spili village. Photoshoot included.
summary: South Crete Highlights is a six-hour private day trip from Rethymno along the south coast of Crete, run daily for groups of up to eight with hotel pick-up at 09:00. The route crosses the Kourtaliotiko Gorge to the cliff-top Preveli Monastery, drops down to the Preveli palm forest where the Megalopotamos River meets the Libyan Sea, stops for swimming and lunch at Triopetra Beach, and finishes with the Venetian lion fountains of Spili village. Difficulty is easy, a professional photoshoot and edited digital album are included, and the price is €250 for a group of up to four.
overview:
South Crete is the unspoiled side of the island, where the mountains run straight down to the sea. The landscape changes constantly along this coast: gorges, rivers, palm groves and quiet beaches that sit well away from the crowds, with small villages scattered across the hills between stone houses, narrow lanes and olive terraces.

Life here is slow. You pass locals going about their day, children playing in the streets and fishermen working along the shore. The air smells of salt, herbs and flowers, and the only soundtrack is waves and birdsong.

This day is built for that pace. You wander, look, swim, eat local food and take your time. It is less a checklist of sights than a chance to feel how the island actually lives, and it works just as well for families as it does for couples.
highlights: Sweeping views of the Libyan Sea from cliff-top Preveli Monastery, and its role in Crete's resistance under Ottoman rule and in the Second World War
A walk through the grove of rare Phoenix theophrasti palms, native to Crete
The lagoon where the Megalopotamos River meets the sea, calm enough to swim in fresh water
The three rocks that give Triopetra Beach its name, rising out of turquoise water
The 25 Venetian lion-head fountains in the square at Spili
A professional photoshoot along the way, delivered as an edited digital album within 48 hours

itinerary.heading: Kourtaliotiko Gorge and Preveli Monastery
itinerary.body: The drive south runs through the Kourtaliotiko Gorge, with a short stop to take in the towering cliffs that rise on either side of the road. From there the road climbs to Preveli Monastery, perched high above the Libyan Sea. The monastery played a significant part in Crete's resistance during the Ottoman era and again in the Second World War, and you will hear what the monks did during both. There is time to walk the Byzantine buildings and the quiet courtyard, which has one of the best sea views on this coast.

itinerary.heading: Preveli Palm Forest
itinerary.body: Next comes the Preveli palm forest, an oasis at the point where the Megalopotamos River reaches the sea. It is one of the few places where the rare Phoenix theophrasti, the Cretan date palm, grows in the wild, which makes the grove an ecological rarity as much as a beauty spot. Walking among the palms you have the sound of the river and the rustle of the fronds, plenty of birdlife, and a lagoon at the end where you can cool off in fresh water before the sea.

itinerary.heading: Triopetra Beach and lunch
itinerary.body: After a scenic drive west along the coast we stop at Triopetra, known for its rock formations and clear turquoise water. The three stones that give the beach its name make a dramatic backdrop against the rugged shoreline, and this is the swimming and photography stop of the day. Lunch is at a taverna nearby with a view over the water; food and drinks are not included in the tour price.

itinerary.heading: Spili village
itinerary.body: On the way back to Rethymno we make a short stop in Spili. The village square is famous for its row of 25 Venetian lion-head fountains running with cold spring water. There is time for a stroll, a coffee and photographs before the drive back down to the coast.

Swimwear under your clothes for the lagoon and the beach
A light layer for the drive through the gorge

faqs.a: Yes, we stop at the historic Preveli Monastery first. The views of the Libyan Sea from the cliffs there are incredible, and the history is even better.

faqs.q: Is this tour okay for kids?
faqs.a: It is perfect for families. Between the palm forest, the waterfalls and the beach, there is always something new to see. It is a fun, active day without being exhausting.

faqs.q: Can we swim in the river?
faqs.a: Definitely. You can walk through the palm forest and then dive into the fresh river water. It is one of the most unique feelings in Crete.
No, comfortable sneakers or good walking sandals are fine. There is a bit of a descent to get to the beach, but nothing too technical.

faqs.q: How much does the tour cost?
faqs.a: €250 for a group of up to four people. Each extra adult beyond four is €50, children aged 4 to 13 are €45 and infants aged 0 to 3 travel free. The group size is capped at eight.
Full refund on cancellations made up to 48 hours before the tour.
